findings.title: retryCount-based deletion is method-agnostic
findings.body: The new `deleteMany` clause `{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }` is placed in the top-level `OR` without any `method` filter, so it will delete EMAIL and WHATSAPP `WorkflowReminder` rows in addition to SMS ones. The rest of the handler only processes SMS (the `findMany` is restricted to `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS`), and only the SMS path increments `retryCount`, so today this is latent — but the schema field is shared and the next contributor who increments `retryCount` for, say, WhatsApp will silently start dropping those rows here. The retry-clause should be scoped to SMS (e.g. `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS, retryCount: { gt: 1 }`) so the deletion rule matches the rule that produces the counter.

findings.title: Retry-based deletion ignores `scheduled` and may drop already-scheduled reminders
findings.body: The `{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }` branch in the top-level `OR` of the `deleteMany` runs without checking `scheduled` or `referenceId`. Today only the failure path increments `retryCount`, so this is latent — but if any future change ever bumps `retryCount` after a successful schedule (for example as part of a send-status callback, or by an SMS_RECEIVED/RECEIPT webhook reconciliation that double-writes), reminders that were already handed off to Twilio will be deleted here while the provider still has a live scheduled message, producing a phantom-delivery bug with no audit row. The retry-deletion should also require `scheduled: false` (or only apply to rows with no `referenceId`) so it cannot tear out rows whose SMS is already in flight.

findings.title: retryCount update uses stale in-memory value (lost-update race)
findings.body: Both the `else` branch (line 179) and the `catch` block (line 190) write `retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1`, where `reminder.retryCount` is the value returned by the `findMany` at the top of the handler. If two cron invocations overlap, or the same reminder is picked up twice within one run, both workers read the same starting value and both write `start + 1`, so the counter only advances by one instead of two. That means under overlap a reminder can take 3–4 actual attempts to reach `retryCount > 1` and be deleted, breaking the "after two failures" guarantee stated in the PR description. The update should be a relative increment (e.g. `{ retryCount: { increment: 1 } }`) so concurrent workers compose correctly.

findings.title: No tests cover the new retry/delete behavior
findings.body: The PR adds a new column, changes the deletion predicate, and introduces two new update sites, but ships no tests for the new behavior. Specifically there is no test covering: (a) `retryCount` increments on `twilio.scheduleSMS` returning a falsy value, (b) `retryCount` increments in the catch block, (c) reminders with `retryCount > 1` are deleted by the next run, (d) reminders with `retryCount <= 1` are not deleted. Without these, a future refactor of the OR/deleteMany/findMany queries could regress the cap without being caught.

findings.title: Error log drops reminder context
findings.body: The catch block only logs `Error scheduling SMS with error ${error}`. It does not include the `reminder.id`, `bookingUid`, `workflowStepId`, or the `sendTo`/recipient, so when the new retry path deletes a reminder after two failures there is no trail in logs tying the deletion back to a specific booking or recipient. For a feature whose entire purpose is to stop silently retrying bad recipients, the error log should at minimum include the reminder id and recipient so on-call can correlate the eventual deletion with the original failure.
